name: Bempedoic acid
route_note: oral tablet once daily, alone or fixed-dose with ezetimibe

discovery.note: Developed by the company founded by Roger Newton, a co-discoverer of atorvastatin. Year of first patent filing (priority January 2003, Esperion, US 7,335,799).

tagline: Liver-activated cholesterol-synthesis blocker for statin-intolerant patients
summary: Bempedoic acid is an oral prodrug that inhibits ATP citrate lyase, an enzyme upstream of HMG-CoA reductase in cholesterol synthesis. It lowers LDL cholesterol by about 20%, and the CLEAR Outcomes trial showed fewer cardiovascular events in statin-intolerant patients.
mechanism: Bempedoic acid is activated to bempedoyl-CoA by very-long-chain acyl-CoA synthetase-1 (ACSVL1), an enzyme present in the liver but largely absent from skeletal muscle.
The active form inhibits ATP citrate lyase, reducing acetyl-CoA supply for cholesterol synthesis. As with statins, lower hepatic cholesterol increases LDL-receptor expression and LDL clearance.
Lack of activation in muscle is thought to explain the low rate of muscle symptoms.
uses: Reduction of cardiovascular risk in adults unable to take recommended statin therapy
Primary hyperlipidaemia including heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia, alone or with other lipid-lowering drugs

history.title: CLEAR Outcomes begins
history.detail: Esperion starts the cardiovascular outcomes trial in statin-intolerant patients that later supports the outcomes label.

history.title: CLEAR Harmony
history.detail: The NEJM reports that bempedoic acid added to maximally tolerated statins lowers LDL cholesterol by about 18% without increasing overall adverse events.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in the US as Nexletol (February) and with ezetimibe as Nexlizet.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: Approved in the EU as Nilemdo and Nustendi, marketed by Daiichi Sankyo Europe.

history.title: CLEAR Outcomes
history.detail: In nearly 14,000 statin-intolerant patients, bempedoic acid reduces major cardiovascular events by 13%.

history.title: Outcomes label
history.detail: The FDA expands the label to cardiovascular risk reduction in adults unable to take recommended statin therapy, including primary prevention in high-risk patients (CLEAR Outcomes).

pk.metabolism: Activated in liver by ACSVL1; glucuronidation

facts: It inhibits the same pathway as statins one step earlier, at ATP citrate lyase.
It raises uric acid by competing for the renal transporter OAT2.
